g.text: Can morphology-driven LCZ subcategorization explain within-class urban thermal exposure inequality at the 100-m neighborhood scale?

text.tspan: Pyatt-Yitzhaki · 6 feature families tested · 5 pp threshold

g.text: Within-class urban thermal exposure inequality is governed by GEOGRAPHIC POSITION
(mountain shading, sea breeze), NOT by building morphology or local topology.
The mechanism is physical, temporally robust, and modulated by city compactness.

svg.text: A 4-stage workstation pipeline for testing whether morphology, topology, or geography explains intra-LCZ heat inequality
